rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: LOLER places duties on people and organisations that own, operate or control lifting equipment used at work.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: Lifting operations must be properly planned by a competent person, appropriately supervised and carried out safely.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: Lifting equipment must be fit for purpose, appropriate for the task and suitably marked.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: Many items of lifting equipment require statutory periodic thorough examination and examination records.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: Defects found during thorough examination must be reported to the responsible person and relevant enforcing authority.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: Lifting equipment must have adequate strength and stability and be positioned to reduce risks from striking, drifting or falling loads.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: Lifting equipment and accessories must be marked with their safe working load and configuration-dependent limits where applicable.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: The complexity and resources of a lifting plan should reflect the complexity and difficulty of the operation.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: Lifting risk depends on equipment type, load, configuration, site, environment, competence, supervision and examination status.

rows.source: HSE lifting operations and lifting-equipment safety
rows.verified: HSE lifting evidence is equipment-, operation-, load-, site-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Scaffolds from which a person might fall 2 metres or more require inspection and a report by a competent person.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Relevant scaffolds should be inspected on completion and at least weekly thereafter.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Risk assessment may require scaffold inspections more frequently than the weekly minimum.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Scaffolds may require inspection after bad weather and must be inspected after modification.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Visible scaffold tags can supplement, but do not replace, the required inspection report.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Scaffolds should be designed, erected, altered and dismantled only by competent people.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Scaffolding work should be directed by a competent supervisor.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Collective fall protection should minimise the time scaffolders are exposed to fall risk and reliance on personal fall protection.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: Scaffold risk depends on design, height, loading, foundations, ties, weather, alteration, inspection and worker competence.

rows.source: HSE scaffolding safety
rows.verified: HSE scaffold evidence is structure-, site-, task-, weather-, inspection- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fall probability.
